points.description: Defines DHCP as a network management protocol in which a DHCP server dynamically assigns an IP address and/or other network configuration to devices. Any wording of this central idea counts, e.g. 'a protocol that automatically gives devices IP addresses'.
points.partial_credit: Half for a vague definition, such as 'a protocol for networks that gives out addresses' with no mention of automatic or dynamic assignment.

points.description: States a use of DHCP: automatically assigning IP addresses or simplifying the installation and configuration of end systems. Any one of the listed uses (manual/automatic address assignment, extra configuration such as DNS server, netmask or default router) is enough.
points.partial_credit: Half for a use that is only loosely described, such as 'it helps set up computers on a network' with no concrete configuration task named.

rubric.notes: Award full marks if the answer says DHCP automatically (dynamically) gives devices an IP address and configuration, and gives at least one use such as simplifying configuration or automatic address assignment. Award half marks for an answer on the right track but vague, for example describing DHCP as a helpful networking protocol without saying what it assigns or what it is used for. Give no marks for an answer that does not describe DHCP's role in assigning addresses or configuration, or that only describes an unrelated protocol. Extra correct detail such as RARP/BOOTP replacement or the specific parameters does not need to be present.
